```{python}
#| label: fig-layout-diff-resistor
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Layout of a diffusion (n-well) resistor: the resistive body is the `NW` strip, contacted at both ends by $n^+$ diffusions (`RX`); the `OP` shape blocks the silicide over the body. The parasitic junction to the substrate makes this resistor nonlinear with the applied voltage."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyutil import laygen as lg

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.0))

# n-well strip forms the resistor body
lg.rect(ax, 'NW', 0, -0.3, 8.6, 2.0)
# n+ diffusion only at the contacted heads; the body is bare n-well
lg.rect(ax, 'RX', 0.3, 0.0, 1.6, 1.4)
lg.rect(ax, 'RX', 6.7, 0.0, 1.6, 1.4)
# silicide block over the body, abutting but not overlapping the heads
lg.rect(ax, 'OP', 1.9, -0.55, 4.8, 2.5)
# contacts + metal
lg.contacts(ax, 0.65, 0.25, 2, 2, pitch=0.55, size=0.35)
lg.contacts(ax, 7.05, 0.25, 2, 2, pitch=0.55, size=0.35)
lg.rect(ax, 'M1', 0.5, 0.1, 1.2, 1.2)
lg.rect(ax, 'M1', 6.9, 0.1, 1.2, 1.2)

ax.text(1.1, -1.0, 'terminal A', fontsize=8, ha='center')
ax.text(7.5, -1.0, 'terminal B', fontsize=8, ha='center')
ax.text(4.3, 0.7, 'n-well body', fontsize=8, ha='center', zorder=10)

lg.legend(ax, ['NW', 'RX', 'OP', 'CA', 'M1'], loc='upper right')
lg.finish(ax, (-0.4, 12.0), (-1.4, 2.6))
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
